Notes and observations from #49ers practice No. 11, a joint joint with the #Titans: - HC Kyle Shanahan took another step in his recovery today, shedding the cast on his left hand in favor of a black brace. He was out there for the whole session and quite involved in the offense. - WR Mike Evans returned from his quad injury. He was in uniform and did some individual stuff but not much else. Spent some time on the bike and exchanged words with some Titans during brief skirmishes. - Warriors GM Mike Dunleavy Jr. was in the house for this one and spent some time chatting with Niners GM John Lynch before practice. - No other changes to the injury list from Monday. Here's the list of non participants: RB Christian McCaffrey (tightness), LB Luke Gifford (hamstring), DE Nick Bosa (soreness), WR Jacob Cowing (hip flexor strain), FB Kyle Juszczyk (broken finger), OL Brett Toth (concussion), WR Christian Kirk (calf), S Malik Mustapha (hamstring), RB Kaelon Black (adductor), RB Jordan James (rib), DL Keion White (adductor), OT Vederian Lowe (ankle) Players on PUP: TE George Kittle (achilles), RB Isaac Guerendo (pec), DL Mykel Williams (ACL) Plenty of them were working on the side, though I didn't see Bosa. McCaffrey and Juszczyk were around a lot with McCaffrey watching practice and offering encouragement. Obviously, no need to rush him back right now. Kyle Shanahan said he was pleased that CMC dialed back at feeling tightness rather than trying to push through it and making it worse. - On Bosa, Shanahan said he is dealing with some tendinitis and soreness in his knee. Shanahan said that's a normal thing for guys coming off ACL surgery and he has no concerns about where Bosa is as it pertains to his return. The goal, of course, is to have their main guys available for Week 1. - Only potential injury issues spotted during practice: DL K.J. Henry was shaken up at one point. Unsure if he returned. OL Carver Willis also limped off favoring his ankle at one point but he quickly returned and finished the practice. - One more injury: Didn't catch which one it was but saw a member of the officiating crew being helped to the training room. Looked like perhaps an accidental collision with a player which led to a pronounced limp. - As a reminder, I only got to see bits and pieces of the Niners defense (see @TDavenport_NFL's timeline for highlights from over there) so much of this will be focused on the Niners offense. And I'll have some special teams notes at the end. - Well documented thing: this session started with A LOT of skirmishes of varying degrees. It was mostly on the other field where the Niners defense was agitating but there were a few close calls on the side for SF's offense as well. One thing that was repeatedly amusing: Any time a fight or near fight broke out near the Niners offense, OT Trent Williams would casually walk in and it would break up fairly quickly. The big fella commands a lot of respect. - It was a bit of a slow start for the offense, particularly in the run game. That could have been due to two things: 1. DT Jeffery Simmons, who remains awesome. 2. The lack of top running backs. After an early run stuff by Simmons, he bellowed "THAT'S WHAT I DO." And, honestly, that IS what he does. Often. - Once things settled in, though, this was a practice with QB Brock Purdy in total control. Not counting him spiking the ball once in two-minute, I had Purdy at 21-of-27 on the day with no interceptions and at least three for sure touchdowns with two or three others that could have gone for one. In one sequence during a move the ball period, Purdy dropped one over and between three defenders to rookie WR De'Zhaun Stribling, hitting him in stride for what likely would have gone for a long touchdown. He then fired a strike to TE Jake Tonges deep down the middle for another big gain as it layered over another defender, fired a short one to WR Deebo Samuel for another chunk and then hit WR Demarcus Robinson on a busted coverage for a touchdown. Even Shanahan had to give Purdy his props after, noting that he had "a hell of a day." - One thing the Titans will need to correct is the penalties. It had to drive Robert Saleh and Gus Bradley crazy seeing the number of flags on their guys today for offsides, defensive pass interference and holding. I counted eight flags on them throughout the practice, the last of which was a defensive pass interference in two minute drill to give the Niners a first down at the 1. - Stribling continues to produce at a high level regardless of who he is on the field with and against. The size and speed are obvious but there's a maturity and understanding of the game that his teammates and coaches continue to notice that are helping him adapt quickly. I had Stribling down for eight catches today in team periods. I'll have more on Stribling and where he might fit in for a story coming soon. - Have said it repeatedly in this camp but will again here: Robinson has really developed a good rapport with Purdy. Those two had another big day today with some deep ones included. There was one rough day last week for that duo but they've otherwise been locked in. - Deebo is getting a lot of work in the back field and at receiver right now and set the tone in this practice a bit with his hard-charging style. His best play of the day: A tremendous one-handed, left-handed catch in the red zone on a ball Purdy threw behind him. Deebo also revved up the run game a bit as practice went on. - Jones and the second unit also had their share of success aside from the one interception (Jones tried to go back shoulder to Jordan Watkins but didn't get it out far enough to that shoulder and the defender jumped in front for the pick). Had Jones at 15-of-19 with particularly strong work in the red zone. In that sequence he found Deebo for a nice gain over the middle then followed with touchdown strikes to Stribling and TE Brayden Willis. The touch throw to Willis in the back of the end zone stood out. - Speaking of Willis, today was his turn to state a case for more of a role and a roster spot. Had him down for five grabs during team periods. Will be curious to see if he can carry it over to games. TE Jake Tonges also made his share of plays today. - Robert Jones continues to work at LG with the top offense with Willis with the 2s. Shanahan mentioned Willis as someone they want to see more of there as the season nears. Willis got flagged for a hold today but otherwise seemed to hold up well. If he can stay on the field, there seems to be a path to playing early. That's a ways off given the time he missed but it exists. - RB Khalil Herbert got the Niners fired up with a red zone run in which he lowered his shoulder, delivered a blow and kept rolling toward the end zone. McCaffrey hustled out to hype Herbert up after the play. - One random thing to like today: On a run play that resulted in Deebo getting the carry, RB Sincere McCormick was charged with acting as his lead blocker. McCormick got to his spot, delivered a well-timed block and opened the hole for a nice gain for Deebo. - To his credit after the fumble early, Turner bounced back late and made a pair of catches from Jones and drew a DPI penalty for Purdy in the final two-minute periods. - Some other Titans defensive notables: After an early completion from QB Mac Jones to WR Malik Turner, Titans CB Micah Robinson forced and recovered a fumble which fired up the Tennessee side. LB Cody Barton had a PBU on a throw from Purdy for WR De'Zhaun Stribling, Simmons got to Purdy for a pressure or would-be sack on a couple of occasions, DE Jermaine Johnson forced a Purdy throwaway, LB Anthony Hill nearly intercepted a pass from Jones for WR Jordan Watkins, DBs Mario Goodrich and Nazeeh Johnson came up with interceptions against Kurtis Rourke and Jones, respectively. - On the special teams front, it's hard to read too much into things right now but here's how the Niners did some things: Corliss Waitman was up first with the punt team with Jack Bouwmeester then getting his turn. Not sure there's much to read into it but we'll see how that goes in preseason games. In the return game, it was Watkins up first as the punt returner with work for Junior Bergen and Will Pauling, among others. - As you might expect, the field with the 49ers offense got done a handful of minutes before the other one. The fighting delayed the work being done there a bit. - Also as you might expect, Shanahan said there won't be many starters playing in the preseason game Thursday. Today serves a similar purpose so the backups will get most of those reps. - That's all for today. Thanks for reading.
